grh_a2c4b9ed6867abe74074.title: War Below Zero
paragraphs: A dramatization of War Below Zero follows American servicemen assigned to isolated weather stations on Greenland's ice cap. Their enemy is primarily cold, blizzards, loneliness and the strain of maintaining weather reports despite months without confirmation that their transmissions are being received. The men continue their work, assist after a bomber crashes in their remote area and eventually learn that their reports did reach command and helped support Allied operations, earning praise before they rotate home for rest.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on July 18, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Paul Mann. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Edith Sommer as radio adaptor, Clifton Fadiman as host, and Jack Costello as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.a811c0d1a6efa194|Johnson's Wax]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.03aac895633e82bc|War Below Zero]]. Bernt Balkan is credited as author, Corey Ford is credited as author, and Edith Sommer adapted it for radio.
